sources.title: Why is the ocean salty?
notes: Weathering of rocks delivers dissolved ions through rivers; hydrothermal systems and underwater volcanism also affect seawater chemistry.

sources.title: Why Is the Ocean Salty?
notes: Sodium and chloride are dominant dissolved ions; average salinity is roughly 35 parts per thousand, varying by region.

sources.title: Why is the ocean salty, but rivers flowing into it are not?
notes: Freshwater continually replenishes rivers while oceans integrate dissolved inputs over time; ocean salinity reflects both sources and removal processes.
